doc.title: Rudy Van Gelder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Musicians who visited to record as a hobby, including Jackie Cooper
summary: Players from bands at the Newark theatre and Benny Goodman's band came to record at his home for little or no charge.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: Was it just your friends or were there some others?

Well it was some friends, and some other musicians would use the theatre in Newark. These bands would appear and a couple of people—a trumpet player, who I know, worked in the band, in one of the bands. So they would come in and visit me and they’d have a band. All sorts of people would come visit me, everyone from Benny Goodman’s band to Jackie Cooper, the drummer. Maureen Sickler Oh so Jackie Cooper came to visit you?
Yeah. He just died not too long ago.
And other musicians, is this about the time that Bill Trillian came in.

Yeah, somewhere around that time, I don’t know exactly, I wasn’t part of how that happened. All I know is that he came to record with me; you mentioned the names. So the phone kept ringing and I kept recording all those years.
And you encouraged them to, you weren’t charging them for…?
Probably some minimum charge, not enough to sustain anything; you know?
